SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: 1-week history of sore throat followed by a dry cough; mild exertional shortness of breath; intermittent wheeze and chest discomfort; low-grade fever for first 3 days (now resolved); intermittent headaches; decreased appetite without weight loss.
- Symptom chronology:
  • Sore throat began last Thu/Fri (≈7 days ago).  
  • Dry cough began 1–2 days later (Sat/Sun).  
  • Shortness of breath started 3–4 days ago, mainly on exertion (able to climb stairs, still exercising).  
  • Fever present first 3 days, now afebrile.  
  • Course described as “up-and-down.”
- Denies sputum production, hemoptysis, nasal congestion, sinus symptoms, rash, or recent significant travel.  
- Past medical history: none reported; no asthma; no thromboembolic disease.
- Family history: mother—lung cancer.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: peanuts.
- Social history: non-smoker (occasional past experimentation only); no known asbestos exposure; moved from US to UK 12 years ago; employed.

Objective:
- Remote video consultation – no vitals or physical examination performed.
- No throat or neck inspection feasible via video; patient reports no palpable neck lumps.
- No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Upper respiratory tract infection / viral pharyngitis with associated dry cough
   - Assessment: Most consistent with self-limiting viral URTI; no red-flag features for pneumonia, tuberculosis, or malignancy identified.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early lower respiratory tract infection, atypical pneumonia, COVID-19 (not tested).
   - Investigations planned: None at this stage; advised to seek in-person review if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Symptomatic care: paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for fever/discomfort.  
     • Adequate oral fluids and rest.  
     • Re-evaluation advised if: increasing breathlessness, new or worsening chest pain, productive or bloody cough, persistent fever, or no improvement within 4–5 days.

2. Fitness for work / sick note
   - Assessment: Ongoing mild symptoms impacting work attendance.
   - Treatment planned: Provide medical certificate for a few additional days off work.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: vitals, objective throat/chest examination, COVID-19 status, complete medication reconciliation (OTC/herbal), vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially denied shortness of breath and chest pain, then later affirmed both (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational overlap but clinically interpretable.
